summary: Expose the smallest complete control set for the current task, group advanced parameters by consequence, and keep hidden state visible through summaries and accessible disclosure controls.
objective: A first-time viewer can perform the primary action and recover from it, while an expert can reveal precise controls without losing keyboard order, state meaning or reset behavior.
applies_when: A 3D experience has many parameters, layers or diagnostics.
Primary actions and advanced tuning should not compete at the same visual level.
intent_signals: hide advanced 3D controls without hiding state
example_prompts: Present play, pause and reset first, then disclose solver and display parameters with a live summary.
Make an advanced material-inspection panel keyboard operable and keep modified hidden values visible.
negative_signals: Collapsing controls while their nondefault effects become invisible.
Using hover-only help as the only explanation of a parameter.
not_for: A fixed onboarding tour required for every scene.

principles: Progressive disclosure changes presentation, not ownership. Collapsed parameters still have explicit values and effects.
The primary layer includes the action, current state and recovery path needed to complete the main task. Advanced layers group controls by consequence rather than implementation module.
Disclosure remains optional and reversible. A user who already understands the scene can skip guidance, and a returning user is not forced through animation.
implementation: In Blender, name controllable objects and author defaults/reference poses; do not encode web control grouping into mesh hierarchy.

In Three.js/DOM, render semantic buttons and disclosure sections. Reflect open state with aria-expanded, optionally connect the controlled region with aria-controls, and support Enter/Space through native button behavior or the documented pattern.
Show a compact summary when a group is collapsed, mark nondefault values, and make reset scope explicit: view, display layer or model state.
observable_checks: Keyboard activation opens and closes each section, focus remains logical, and collapsed content does not leave unreachable focused controls.
Change an advanced value, collapse the group, and verify its effect and nondefault summary remain apparent; scoped reset restores only the declared state.
At the smallest supported viewport, the primary action, current state and recovery path remain reachable without the advanced panel covering the scene.

creative_affordances: Use drawers, accordions, command palettes or staged prompts to fit the experience.
Advanced controls may be always visible in an expert workspace when hierarchy remains clear.
known_limits: The WAI APG disclosure pattern describes control semantics, not which application controls should be advanced.
No keyboard, screen-reader, onboarding or persistence test was run.

claims.statement: The WAI ARIA Authoring Practices disclosure pattern uses a button controlling hidden/visible content, toggles it with Enter or Space, reflects state with aria-expanded, and may identify the controlled region with aria-controls.
claims.scope: Disclosure widget semantics; control grouping and default openness remain authored choices.
